strategies.name: Baseline unrolled 8-stage all-reduce
strategies.desc: Direct translation of the reference implementation with 8 sequential all-reduce calls, each preceded by bidiagonal coupling and followed by inverse coupling. 8 all-reduce dispatches on full W*S payload. Represents the naive baseline with maximum dispatch overhead but simplest logic.

strategies.name: Fused bidirectional coupling computation
strategies.desc: Merge the forward coupling and backward inverse coupling into a single vectorized operation per stage, reducing local compute overhead. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but with optimized local ops that can be fused by XLA compiler. Trades code complexity for reduced local arithmetic dispatch count.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction tree
strategies.desc: Exploit the 224=32×7 factorization to first perform intra-group reductions (32 groups of 7), apply bidiagonal transformations at group level, then inter-group reductions. Approximately 16 collective dispatches (8 stages × 2 levels) on smaller payloads. Trades more collectives for reduced per-dispatch bandwidth.

strategies.name: Pipelined overlapped stages
strategies.desc: Split the W*S tensor into chunks and pipeline the 8 stages so that stage k+1 begins on chunk i while stage k processes chunk i+1. Uses async all-reduce primitives with explicit token management. Total dispatches remain 8×num_chunks but allows overlap of communication and computation, hiding latency.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pattern
strategies.desc:
Use reduce-scatter to distribute W shards of size S across ranks, perform all 8 bidiagonal coupling stages locally on scattered data with point-to-point exchanges for boundary values, then all-gather to reconstruct full result. Approximately 2 + 8×2 = 18 dispatches (reduce-scatter, 8×send/recv pairs, all-gather) but exploits smaller per-rank working set.
